brief: Goldman's morning client wrap covers five live themes. On oil, Gulf exports (including estimated 'dark exports') have recovered near 2025-average levels and the market looks balanced, supporting GS's base case of Brent easing to $85/bbl by year-end and $80 in 2027, though renewed escalation damaging energy infrastructure is flagged as an upside risk; LNG recovery lags oil's, and futures positioning in energy looks stretched and vulnerable to a flush-out. Separately, bonds are not yet a reliable risk-off hedge because energy-driven yields still weigh on equities; resolving the Iran conflict is seen as the quickest path back to that hedge. On Brazil, GS recommends receiving the DI curve into the October 4 election, arguing downside from a fiscally unfriendly result would be smaller than upside from a market-friendly one, despite elevated debt and a tight race. On Q3 earnings, consensus 27% S&P EPS growth (down from 33% last quarter) is expected to beat, with 2027 AI capex guided at $1.25-1.5tn against very light positioning that skews risk upside. On the UK, EU reintegration options could reverse part of a ~6% Brexit GDP hit, though near-term asset impact stays limited. GS Asia also recommends receiving Korea rates and paying CNH/MYR swaps on country-specific disinflation, appreciation-limit and rate-hike themes.
